# Severity and declaration

Use this reference when the request asks how serious the incident is, whether to declare, who must
be paged, or how often updates are due. The `incident-command` entrypoint's security carve-out and
human-only effect boundary remain controlling.

## Severity rubric — round up when unsure

| Tier | Definition (user impact × scope) | What it triggers |
|---|---|---|
| **P1 — Critical** | Customer-facing outage for all or most users, **or** a data-loss, integrity, or security event | Declare now; assign an incident commander; page on-call, service owner, and leadership; status updates every **15 minutes**; full blameless postmortem |
| **P2 — High** | Major degradation, or one critical service or journey down for a subset of users | Declare; assign an incident commander; page on-call and service owner; updates every **30 minutes**; postmortem required |
| **P3 — Medium** | Minor or contained impairment; core journeys work or a workaround exists | On-call owns the lifecycle; no IC required; update stakeholders at start and resolution; abbreviated postmortem |
| **P4 — Low** | Cosmetic or informational; no user impact | Normal work queue; no incident process |

This is the fleet's canonical P1-P4 ladder and cadence, ratified by the owner on 2026-08-23.
*[sourced: owner ratification]*

## Classify from impact, scope, and trend

- **Impact:** What fails for one affected user or business journey? Name data loss or integrity risk
  separately from availability.
- **Scope:** How many users, journeys, routes, regions, apps, or instances are affected? State the
  denominator when a percentage is available.
- **Trend:** Say whether impact is growing, steady, or recovering. A growing P3 is escalating toward
  P2; re-page rather than waiting for the next cadence.

Set the first severity from available evidence and mark it provisional. If the blast radius cannot
yet be bounded, that uncertainty alone justifies P2 and declaration.

For PCF/TAS evidence, one affected app, route, or instance is likely app-side. Many apps failing at
once, or evidence of failing or evacuating Diego cells, is platform-shaped and must be escalated to
the platform team. Capture bounded, sanitized `cf apps`, `cf app`, `cf events`, and
`cf logs --recent` evidence or hand the collection request to the typed `sre` agent; do not cross
the platform boundary yourself.

The first responder time-box is about ownership, not certainty: if service is not stabilized in
roughly 15 minutes, or impact is growing, declare and assign an incident commander. Do not keep
digging solo.

Suspected compromise, data integrity loss, or another security event is at least P1 for declaration
purposes, but the entrypoint's evidence-preservation carve-out controls mitigation. Immediately
escalate to the human security incident owner and take no state-changing action unless that owner
directs the exact action.
